item.title: Hi Marley Launches Unite Service Provider Network
item.description: Hi Marley says Unite lets carriers extend the Hi Marley conversation across their service provider network while maintaining control of the policyholder experience. (Image source: Hi Marley website.) Hi Marley (Boston) has launched Unite, an insurance-specific conversational network designed to help property/casualty carriers coordinate communication across service providers. Unite brings approved service-provider communication into the same Hi Marley conversation policyholders already use for a claim, according to a Hi Marley statement.

item.title: New Security Incidents: OpenAI, Anthropic AI Agents Implicated
item.description: The institute said agents powered by Anthropic’s Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6-Sol engaged in unauthorized actions during security evaluations the government organization conducted to assess the models’ capabilities. An AI agent was caught creating fake online identities to gain unauthorized access to secure systems during tests of models from OpenAI and Anthropic which revealed a series of new breaches, Britain’s AI Security Institute disclosed on Tuesday. Anthropic’s agent was behind 17 of the actions, and OpenAI’s agent the remaining two.

item.title: Another M&A Deal: AXIS Acquiring DUAL NA XS Liability Biz
item.description: AXIS said that John Kopach, executive vice president of DUAL Excess Liability, will join AXIS as part of the terms of the deal. AXIS Capital announced that it has agreed to acquire the renewal rights to the excess liability business of DUAL North America (“DUAL”). “This transaction reflects the strong partnership and strategic relationship that AXIS shares with DUAL, and we are enthused to add this high-quality Excess Liability book to our Casualty platform,” said McKenna.

item.title: Side Underride Guards on Trucks Prevent Deaths
item.description: Side underride crashes kill 300 annually, yet the trucking industry still resists guards that juries now value in multimillion-dollar verdicts. Riley's crash was one of roughly 300 deaths and 400 serious injuries that side underride causes each year, with an estimated societal cost of $7.4 billion. Side underride guards, like seat belts and airbags, reduce the severity of consequences regardless of fault.

item.title: Agency Growth Numbers May Be Misleading You
item.description: I spend a lot of time with agency principals at very different stages of growth. Revenue growth masks a retention crisis costing agencies millions in enterprise value and leaving half their book vulnerable to churn. The insurance distribution industry has spent years treating enrollment volume as the definitive signal of agency health.

item.title: Starwind launches high-net-worth builders risk program
item.description: CRC Group’s Starwind has launched Starwind Private Client, a new underwriting platform focused on high-net-worth individuals and families with complex residential property risks. The platform debuts with Private Client Construction, a standalone owner-named builders risk product for custom home construction and renovations with completed values of up to $30 million. According to Starwind, the program is designed for ground-up construction, major renovations, additions, repairs, rebuilds following homeowner losses, catastrophe-exposed properties, and other complex luxury residential projects that often fall outside standard underwriting appetite.

item.title: Root reports Q2 2026 results
item.description: Root Insurance released its Q2 2026 results, ending the period with ~484k policies-in-force, a 6% increase compared to Q2 2025. As of June 30, 2026, Root had $509.6 million in cash and cash equivalents, of which $239.5 million was held outside of regulated insurance entities. Root’s policy count fell by 11,508 during the quarter.

item.title: Sompo to sponsor new PGA TOUR Championship Series event
item.description: Sompo Holdings has signed a multi-year agreement with the PGA TOUR to become the title sponsor of a full-field tournament beginning in 2027, with the event transitioning into the new PGA TOUR Championship Series in 2028. Beginning in 2028, the tournament will relocate to a new market tha t has yet to be announced as part of the PGA TOUR’s new Championship Series. The sponsorship follows a series of strategic investments by Sompo in 2026, including agreements to acquire Service Insurance Companies, a U.S.

item.title: INTX Launches Tenet Intelligence Layer
item.description: (Image source: INTX.) INTX Insurance Software (Austin, Texas) has launched Tenet, an intelligence layer embedded within the company’s unified reinsurance and insurance operating platform. Tenet is designed to bring contextual intelligence across underwriting, reinsurance, policy administration, claims, accounting and financial operations, according to an INTX statement. Tenet is the natural evolution of that architecture, delivering intelligence with the full context of the business—not just individual tasks or documents.” Tenet operates across the INTX platform, including ReinsureConnect, INTX Re and INTX Core.

item.title: Solertia Selects Optalitix Underwriting Workbench
item.description: (Image source: Solertia Insurance website.) Solertia Insurance (London) has selected Optalitix (London) to deliver a cloud-based underwriting workbench for its specialty insurance operations. Solertia, a Lloyd’s coverholder and specialist MGA, will use Optalitix Quote to replace its previous underwriting system with a fully integrated platform bringing underwriting workflows, reporting and operational activity into one place, according to an Optalitix statement. The new workbench is intended to reduce manual administration, improve operational visibility and give Solertia flexibility to adapt underwriting processes as the business grows.

item.title: Citigroup Settles $70 Million Trade-Loss Suit With Loomis Sayles
item.description: Boston-based Loomis Sayles sued in 2022, claiming it lost money in a series of trades on March 18 in which Citigroup’s global markets unit acted as its broker. The case is Loomis Sayles v Citigroup Global Markets Inc. has resolved a lawsuit filed four years ago by Loomis, Sayles & Co.

item.title: Google Loses Bid to Block UK Class Action Over Search Ads
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google must face a class action lawsuit over alleged abuse of its dominance after an antitrust tribunal allowed a claim on behalf of hundreds of thousands of British firms to go ahead. The lawsuit alleged that Google overcharged businesses that paid for online advertising and abused its dominance over mobile operating systems, app distribution and search advertising. The Competition Appeal Tribunal on Wednesday rejected Google’s bid to block the claim.

item.title: Lawsuits Over Child Safety, Deaths Mount Against Social Media Firms
item.description: The lawsuit, filed Thursday in the Superior Court of Delaware, is the latest in a flurry of suits filed against the social media giants that allege their platforms are addictive and dangerous. “This is a clear and present danger to the health and safety of children, not just in the United States but around the world.” The four teens who died by suicide each experienced harms including social media addiction, severe sleep deprivation, depression, anxiety and suicidal ideation after years of using the social platforms, the complaint states. The families of four teenagers who died by suicide are suing Meta, TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube over what they describe as “years of escalating harms” from using their platforms that eventually resulted in their deaths.

item.title: Business Uncertainty Drives Changes in C-Suite Strategy: Sentry
item.description: Economic uncertainty—fueled by shifting trade policies, geopolitical instability, and operational disruptions—is driving leaders to rethink planning, risk management, and long-term strategy, according to new research from Sentry Insurance. New data from a survey of more than 600 executives reveals that C-suite confidence has fallen sharply since the start of 2026, with 82% of U.S. executives more concerned about the future of their business than at the beginning of the year.

item.title: Key to Customer Loyalty in Claims Journey Mixes AI and Human Judgment
item.description: A new report by Deloitte examined nearly 4,000 auto and home policyholder responses detailing where insurers can improve the claims journey without losing the human touch. Combining AI and human judgment can lower friction during the claims process, according to the authors, who include managing director and a leader in the insurance sector claims practice Kedar Kamalapurkar, Malika Gandhi principal in Deloitte Consulting’s Insurance practice, firm specialist executive manager at the Deloitte Center for Financial Services Namrata Sharma, and Sabyasachi Satapathy, senior manager in insurance transformation, AI, and engineering at Deloitte Consulting. The analysis across 12 property and casualty insurance carriers examined eight variables that most influence customer sentiment and future purchase intentions: the claims process, service speed, claims outcome, communication, attitude, knowledge, customer support, and app or website.

item.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
item.description: Methodology This tracker includes layoffs conducted by U.S.-based companies or those with a strong U.S. We source the layoffs from media reports, our own reporting, social media posts and layoffs.fyi , a crowdsourced database of tech layoffs. We recently updated our layoffs tracker to reflect the most recent round of layoffs each company has conducted.

item.title: CatIQ finalises industry loss estimate for 2024 Calgary hailstorm at C$3.34bn
item.description: CatIQ, Canada’s insured loss and exposure indices provider, has published a final insurance industry loss estimate of CAD $3.34 billion for the severe hailstorm that struck Calgary, Alberta Canada on August 5th, 2024. We also covered the firm’s fourth loss estimate of $3.25 billion, which was issued six months after the event, as well as CatIQ’s first loss estimate from the hailstorm in September 2024, where losses had surpassed $2.8 billion., CatIQ also confirmed that its loss estimate covers property (both commercial and residential) and vehicle (motor) claims including additional loss adjustment expenses. “So, while the 2024 event progressed more slowly through the first year, the industry has largely caught up at the two-year mark, despite handling nearly twice the claim volume of the 2020 storm.” At the same time, CatIQ has also published an initial loss estimate of $374 million for the severe thunderstorm event that impacted parts of southern Ontario and southern Quebec between June 30th and July 3rd, 2026, “Several days of strong thunderstorms capped off a heatwave that had gripped the region at the end of June, with widespread reports of flash flooding, hail up to 40 mm in diameter, and at least two confirmed tornadoes”, CatIQ explained.

item.title: CSU maintains well below-normal hurricane forecast. Landfall probabilities down as season progresses
item.description: The Colorado State University (CSU) tropical meteorology team has stuck with its forecast of well-below normal activity levels for the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season , while its landfall probability metrics have declined somewhat as the season progresses. The CSU forecast team commented today, “We have maintained our 2026 Atlantic basin hurricane season forecast for a well below- normal season. We are forecasting a well below-average probability for major hurricane landfalls along the continental United States coastline and in the Caribbean.” The expectations of meteorological and climatic conditions remain unchanged, with the strong El Nino and expected notable increase in vertical wind shear still the main factors for the well-below normal hurricane season forecast.

item.title: James Hebert named Head of US Financial Lines, Rokstone
item.description: Rokstone, an international specialty re/insurance managing general agent (MGA), has appointed James Hebert as Head of US Financial Lines to lead the launch of its new US Errors & Omissions (E&O) Division. Ian Anson, Chief Executive Officer, Rokstone, commented on the appointment, “James is one of the most respected financial lines leaders in the US market. In his new role, Hebert will be based in New York and will lead the build out of the new division, bringing extensive underwriting expertise, deep broker relationships, and a proven track record in building successful financial lines portfolios.

item.title: Antares announces new leadership structure, Tabbakh to oversee Global business
item.description: Antares Global, an international specialty insurance and reinsurance group, has announced a new leadership structure, with Ahmed El Tabbakh, QIC’s Group Chief Business Officer – International, assuming the oversight of the business. Under the new structure, several functions that were previously shared, notably Claims, Actuarial, Compliance and Risk, as well as certain operational functions, will be divided to offer direct assistance to the separate Antares Retail and Antares Commercial business units. The restructured organisation will maintain key leadership across its core business units while refining executive roles.

item.title: CatIQ closes book on record 2024 Calgary hailstorm with CAD 3.35bn industry loss estimate
item.description: Catastrophe Indices and Quantification Inc (CatIQ), the independent Toronto-based organisation that provides industry-wide catastrophe insurance data and is a subsidiary of PERILS, has disclosed its sixth and final industry loss estimate for the hailstorm that struck Calgary, Alberta, Canada, on 5 August 2024, at around CAD 3.35bn. So, while the 2024 event progressed more slowly through the first year, the industry has largely caught up at the two-year mark, despite handling nearly twice the claim volume of the 2020 storm.” In addition, CatIQ has issued an initial industry loss estimate for the severe thunderstorm event that affected southern Ontario and Quebec in early July 2026, alongside its 45-day post-event update for the June 2026 flooding event that impacted Montreal’s West Island. This figure is broadly unchanged from CatIQ’s one-year post-event estimate of CAD 3.293bn , while representing a slight increase from the fourth estimate of CAD 3.25bn issued six months after the event.

item.title: LDI Introduces One-Time Process for Military Auto Insurance Discount
item.description: The Louisiana Department of Insurance has revised the application process for military members to receive a 25% discount on the liability portion of their auto insurance premium. “This law recognizes their service by helping military members save on auto insurance,” Temple said in a statement. “I made this change with the intent to incentivize more of our service members to take advantage of this significant discount.” In order to receive the discount, active-duty military personnel and military reservists must provide current military orders showing assignment to a duty station in Louisiana .

item.title: Amazon’s Zoox to Levy Fares, in US First for Controls-Free Taxis in Vegas
item.description: Amazon.com Inc.’s Zoox robotaxi division will start charging fares next week in Las Vegas, marking a first in the U.S. Related: Amazon’s Zoox Wins First US Approval for Paid Robotaxis Without Human Controls The full fare will be visible to riders prior to booking. Zoox will charge Vegas customers starting Aug.

item.title: Jury Says Medtronic Owes $88 Million in First Trial Over Covidien’s Hernia Mesh
item.description: Medtronic must pay an Alabama man and his wife $88 million, a federal jury decided on Tuesday, in the first case to go to trial out of thousands facing the company from people claiming they were injured by hernia-repair mesh implants made by one of its units. Patterson’s case is the first bellwether, or test case, to go to trial of thousands of cases against Medtronic, the last major body of litigation over hernia mesh after other companies, including units of Becton Dickinson and Johnson & Johnson, largely settled cases against them. “We remain confident in Covidien’s hernia mesh products, as over the past two decades these products have been used safely and effectively in millions of patients, and hernia mesh has long been the standard of care for repair of all but the smallest hernia defects,” Medtronic said in a statement.

item.title: Guidewire launches AI agent framework to automate insurance workflows
item.description: Rather than simply generating responses or summaries, Guidewire’s framework allows AI agents to interact with operational systems and complete tasks within existing insurance workflows. Insurance software provider Guidewire has launched an Agentic Framework as part of its new Qusar release, enabling insurers to build, deploy and manage AI agents directly within the Guidewire Cloud Platform. The new capability is designed to bring autonomous AI systems into core insurance workflows, including policy administration, claims, billing, underwriting and software development, allowing carriers to automate complex processes while maintaining governance, security and regulatory controls.

item.title: Talcott launches $1 billion reinsurance sidecar with Goldman Sachs
item.description: Talcott Financial Group has launched West Grove Re, a Bermuda-domiciled reinsurance sidecar established in partnership with Goldman Sachs, raising approximately $1 billion through equity commitments from Talcott, Goldman Sachs Asset & Wealth Management and its clients, along with a credit facility. Talcott will provide the sidecar with actuarial, finance, compliance, risk management, and other support services, while Goldman Sachs Asset & Wealth Management will oversee private asset investment strategies. The company manages $134 billion in assets as of March 31, 2026, while Goldman Sachs Alternatives oversees more than $706 billion in alternative assets globally and approximately $508 billion in insurance assets under supervision.

item.title: Hagerty: 2027 should reveal underlying earnings power
item.description: 2027 should reveal the company’s true earnings power Management repeatedly emphasized that 2026 remains distorted by accounting changes associated with the Markel fronting transition. Those temporary items disappear next year, leaving financial results that more closely reflect Hagerty’s underlying premium growth and operating leverage. Hagerty reported a first-half net loss of $5 million, compared with net income of $74 million a year earlier.

item.title: Mutual of Omaha pilots AI automation with Vamrah
item.description: Mutual of Omaha’s Workplace Solutions business is partnering with AI automation company Vamrah to pilot artificial intelligence tools designed to automate business processes across its group insurance operations. Vamrah develops AI software for enterprise workflow automation, with a focus on document processing and unstructured data. The initiative focuses on reducing repetitive manual work and streamlining group insurance workflows through AI-powered automation.

item.title: EEOC Moves to End Employer Reporting of Worker Race, Sex Data
item.description: agency that enforces laws banning workplace discrimination moved to scrap a requirement that employers annually submit data on the race and sex of their workers, which since its adoption in the 1960s has been a cornerstone of civil rights enforcement. But EEOC Chair Andrea Lucas, an appointee of Republican President Donald Trump, said that sorting workers by race and sex can fuel discrimination, including against majority groups such as white people and men. The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, led by Republican appointees, voted 2-1 to publish a proposed rule that would end the practice, known as EEO-1 reporting, named for the forms that companies with 100 or more employees have been compelled to complete since 1966.

This will allow the UK listings market to compete more effectively with global markets. These changes support the FCA's aim of enabling growth, investment and innovation, while continuing to uphold high standards of market integrity and investor protection.

item.title: Your AI Strategy May Be Destroying Your Exit Value
item.description: Let’s jump into three ways AI strategy can impact exit value. While I agree that for some companies this may be true, in other cases I think it may actually be destroying the company’s value. AI does not automatically increase exit value.

item.title: ‘Nobody Wanted to Give A Former Principal Money’: How An Educator Built An Edtech AI Startup With $63M From VCs
item.description: Editor’s note: The following is the first profile in a series of articles in coming weeks about startup founders from non-technical backgrounds who have launched successful venture-backed companies. In November 2022, Adeel Khan was doing something rare for a longtime educator: taking time off. Having launched his career as a teacher in Atlanta Public Schools, Khan became an assistant principal before founding his own public high school in Denver.

item.title: Willis executes “Dynamic Cat-in-Circle” parametric policy for Caribbean coral reef
item.description: Willis, a business of insurance and reinsurance broker WTW, and the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF) have launched a market-first “Dynamic Cat-in-Circle” parametric insurance policy to protect Caribbean coral reefs. Additional concentric circles with lower payouts further align cover with a hurricane’s wind footprint.” Kaniescka Yogeswaran, Manager, Alternative Risk Transfer Solutions, Willis, commented: “Helping to design the first ‘Dynamic Cat-in-Circle’ parametric policy for coral reefs in the Caribbean has been a rewarding challenge. As mentioned, the parametric policy introduces a “Dynamic Cat-in-Circle” structure that considerably reduces “near miss” hurricane events present in traditional Cat-in-Circle policies.

item.title: PCC structure will be a game changer for Singapore’s ILS landscape: Rajah & Tann’s Goh
item.description: As Singapore continues to work on plans to adopt a regulatory framework for a Protected Cell Company (PCC) structure to support collateralised reinsurance and ILS issuance, Simon Goh of law firm Rajah & Tann Singapore, has expressed how this flexible structure could ultimately become a game changer for the country’s captive insurance and ILS landscape. Given this, Artemis recently spoke to Simon Goh who leads Rajah & Tann Singapore’s Insurance & Reinsurance Practice, who shared how he feels this structure will impact the country’s ILS landscape. Whilst speaking to Artemis about Singapore’s new plans for a PCC structure, Goh explained why he thinks this flexible ILS structure could become a game changer for Singapore.

item.title: Third-party capital helps Hiscox’s market relevance, expands underwriting capacity: CUO Musselle
item.description: Hiscox Re, the reinsurance operation and third-party capital platform of Hiscox Ltd, continues to utilise its Capital Partners division to gain further relevance in the market, and deploy more underwriting capabilities, according to Hiscox Group Chief Underwriting Officer (CUO), Joanne Musselle. “Scaling Hiscox Capital Partners, so, third-party capital gives us both relevance in the market, but it also enables us to deploy more of our underwriting capability than our own balance sheet would allow, and this builds attractive portfolios for our partners and fee income for ourselves,” the CUO explained. Meanwhile during his opening remarks, Aki Hussain, CEO of Hiscox, highlighted how Hiscox Re’s underwriting and risk selecting continues to attract third-party capital providers.

item.title: More standardisation of terms, but reinsurance retentions held in H1’26: Hiscox CUO
item.description: After highlighting some modest softening in terms and conditions (T&Cs) witnessed by Hiscox Re in the first half of 2026, Hiscox Group Chief Underwriting Officer (CUO), Joanne Musselle, said recently that while the firm’s ability to carve out differentiated terms has lessened, importantly, retentions held. The firm’s earnings release noted how Hiscox is “managing net natural catastrophe exposures at this point in the cycle,” which led to net ICWP at Hiscox Re falling 7.4% to $381.1 million, driven by the aforementioned reduction in catastrophe exposures, which more than offset growth in other areas. So, third-party capital gives us both relevance in the market, but it also enables us to deploy more of our underwriting capability than our own balance sheet would allow, and this builds attractive portfolios for our partners and fee income for ourselves.” The reinsurance business saw strong third-party capital support across traditional quota share partners and insurance-linked securities (ILS), with ILS assets under management up by $1.4 billion to $2.9 billion at July 1st, 2026.

item.title: CLARA Analytics launches new integration between its Triage platform and CLARA DocIntel Pro
item.description: CLARA Analytics, a provider of artificial intelligence (AI) technology for commercial insurance claims optimisation, has introduced new integration between its market-leading Triage platform and CLARA DocIntel Pro. This isn’t just about reading a document; it’s about allowing document-level insights to actively drive better claims decisions.” The latest enhancements to its Triage platform and DocIntel Pro solution enable claims professionals to access more comprehensive data, identify complex claims earlier and review medical records more efficiently without requiring additional training or changes to existing processes. This is the industry’s first true unification of document intelligence and predictive claims analytics on a singular platform, demonstrating an automated data path to convert unstructured medical and legal files into active claims-driving insights.

item.title: Willis and CBF launch first-of-its-kind coral reef parametric insurance programme
item.description: Willis, a WTW business, and the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF) have launched a first-of-its-kind parametric insurance programme to protect Caribbean coral reefs. Kaniescka Yogeswaran, Manager, Alternative Risk Transfer Solutions, Willis, said, “Helping to design the first ‘Dynamic Cat-in-Circle’ parametric policy for coral reefs in the Caribbean has been a rewarding challenge. With climate change-related natural hazards increasing in scale and frequency, this type of ground-breaking solution enables the rapid deployment of resources to help repair critical ecosystems and restore services following a major event like a hurricane.” Karen McDonald Gayle, CEO of the Caribbean Biodiversity Fund, added, “The Caribbean Biodiversity Fund is thrilled to pilot this world-first coral reef insurance policy.

item.title: AI Now Fuels Over Half of Africa’s Cybercrime, Study Finds
item.description: Artificial intelligence is fueling more than half of cybercrime in Africa, enabling criminals to launch faster, more sophisticated attacks as financial losses continue to mount, a new study found. The study found that one of the fastest-growing threats to Africa is the creation of AI-generated synthetic identities that combine genuine personal information with fabricated details. “Cybercrime has emerged as one of the most significant criminal threats to the region,” Neal Jetton, director of Interpol’s Cybercrime Directorate, said in a report released Monday that surveyed 36 countries.

item.title: German DHL Cargo Plane Hits Object as Drone Found at Leipzig Airport
item.description: Drone Found Near Leipzig/Halle Airport Runway Bild reported that a drone with a n explosive device had been found lying in the immediate vicinity of a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane shortly before midnight on Tuesday. A DHL cargo aircraft hit an unknown object as it was climbing away from Leipzig/Halle airport in eastern Germany overnight, prompting an unscheduled landing in Hanover, a source familiar with the incident told Reuters on Wednesday. Authorities said they were investigating a drone found near a runway at the airport during the night, which the Bild newspaper said contained a detonator.

item.title: Law Restricts Her From Reducing ‘Excessive’ $91M Injured Worker Award, Judge Finds
item.description: A Massachusetts judge has declined to reduce the $91 million damages award she approved last September for a construction worker’s personal injury claim, an award she herself characterized as “grossly excessive” but found is required by statute and precedent. Suffolk Superior Court Justice Debra Squires-Lee found that because Liberty Mutual insurers willfully failed to investigate and make a reasonable offer to injured worker John Rooney, she was obligated under state law to at least double the verdict issued by a jury in August 2021. In addition to citing the insurer’s failures in investigating and negotiating offers, the judge suggested Liberty was also hurt by failing to argue that such a large award raised constitutional issues even though it was put on notice that it could face such a large award.

item.title: Allianz expands Asia strategy with UOB Asset Management acquisition
item.description: Allianz SE has agreed to acquire United Overseas Bank’s asset management business for S$555 million (US$433 million) , strengthening its asset management presence in Asia as the German insurer continues its regional expansion strategy. The acquisition also aligns with Allianz’s broader strategy of increasing its exposure to asset management. The acquisition, announced Wednesday, will see Allianz Global Investors (AllianzGI) purchase UOB Asset Management Ltd.

item.title: Diesta integrates Kinexys payee verification into insurance payment platform
item.description: “By integrating Kinexys Liink’s Confirm application into Diesta, we are bringing account and payee verification directly into the insurance payment workflow. Morgan’s Kinexys Liink Confirm application into its insurance payment platform, enabling insurers, brokers and managing general agents (MGAs) to verify beneficiary account details before payments are made. The integration brings account and payee verification directly into insurance payment workflows, addressing a longstanding challenge in commercial insurance where high-value payments often pass through multiple parties, currencies and banking systems and still rely heavily on manual validation processes.

item.title: IKEA launches home insurance in the UK through Urban Jungle partnership
item.description: IKEA has entered the UK insurance market through a partnership with London-based insurtech Urban Jungle , offering home insurance products to customers as the retailer expands its “Life at Home” services. The partnership marks Urban Jungle’s first collaboration with IKEA in the UK and extends the startup’s AI-powered insurance platform to a broader customer base. By partnering with Urban Jungle, we are bringing a simple, functional and affordable home insurance product to our customers, ensuring they have peace of mind that their homes and belongings are protected.” The launch reflects the growing trend of non-insurance brands embedding financial protection products into their customer offerings, as retailers increasingly look to expand beyond their traditional product portfolios through digital partnerships.

item.title: Corbel, Sea Pine invest in Executive Exteriors
item.description: Corbel Capital Partners and Sea Pine Equity Partners have invested in Texas-based roofing and exterior restoration company Executive Exteriors. Corbel and Sea Pine share our commitment to our people, our customers and our culture, and together we’re investing in the next phase of growth while continuing to build on the foundation that got us here.” – Drake Gordon, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Executive Exteriors. Founded in 2018, Executive Exteriors provides specialty roofing, exterior restoration, and insurance claim support services to residential and commercial customers.

item.title: IKEA launches home insurance in the UK
item.description: London-based insurance startup Urban Jungle has partnered with IKEA to launch a home insurance offering for customers across the UK. We believe in fair insurance for everyone, and by joining forces with Ikea, we can bring our technology driven, AI powered accessible home insurance to an even wider audience. We are proud to be the first insurance provider to collaborate with Ikea in the UK, offering insurance that truly puts the customer first.” – Jimmy Williams, CEO and Co-Founder at Urban Jungle.

item.title: Edison Equipment Blamed for Deadly Eaton Fire in Los Angeles
item.description: Southern California Edison equipment sparked a January 2025 wildfire that killed 19 people in the Los Angeles area, fire officials said. “We have taken our potential role in the start of this fire seriously from the beginning.” Related: California Utility Has Offered $750M in Program for Eaton Fire Victims Last week, Edison Chief Executive Officer Pedro Pizzaro told investors that “no other viable alternatives have appeared” aside from the company’s equipment that would explain how the wildfire erupted. The Eaton Fire was caused by electrical arcing events that took place on an out-of-service tower on a dry hillside, the Los Angeles County Fire Department said in a statement Tuesday.
